NDT training in Houston: how it works for Houston employers and technicians

NDT training in Houston is delivered by Atlantis NDT as ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based Level I, II and III courses in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET — live online for technicians anywhere in Texas, or onsite at your plant, yard or shop under ASNT Level III oversight. Your employer then certifies you under its written practice once training, documented experience, examinations and a vision test are complete.

That one paragraph hides the detail that matters most in Houston: under SNT-TC-1A, a course does not certify anybody on its own. The certificate belongs to the employer. It is issued under the employer’s written practice, and it is only valid while you work for that employer. A Houston contractor bidding a turnaround, a fabrication shop in north Harris County shipping pressure vessels, and an oilfield-equipment maker qualifying its inspectors all run their own written practice. Training is the input they need to issue a certificate, not the certificate itself.

So there are two kinds of reader here. Employers — inspection contractors, owner-operators, fabricators, machine shops and OEMs across Greater Houston — need Level I and Level II technicians trained to the hours their written practice requires, examined by a Level III and documented well enough to survive a client audit. Individual technicians need the classroom hours and exam preparation that make them hireable, plus a clear picture of how the experience hours and employer certification will follow. We serve both. There is no Atlantis classroom building to drive to on the Katy Freeway or the Gulf Freeway. The classroom is on your screen or at your facility. For crews spread across the Ship Channel, Freeport, Beaumont–Port Arthur and the Permian Basin, that is usually quicker than getting everyone to one room.

If you already know what you need, request a Houston training quote. You will get cohort and onsite quotes within one business day. Otherwise, read on. The rest of this section covers each method, the certification path, delivery options, Texas radiography licensing and the questions Houston candidates ask most.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in Houston

Each course follows the SNT-TC-1A recommended structure for its method and level. The course covers the physics, equipment, calibration, technique, interpretation and codes that the general and specific examinations draw on, plus supervised practical work. The Houston table below maps each method to the local work it feeds. That tells you which course to take first.

MethodLevelsWhat Houston employers use it forPrerequisite
Ultrasonic Testing (UT)I, II, IIIThickness readings at condition-monitoring locations on process piping, shear-wave weld examination on ASME B31.3 piping and ASME Section VIII vessels, lamination checks on plate at fabrication shopsNone for Level I; Level II needs Level I plus documented experience per your written practice
Phased Array UT (PAUT)I, IICorrosion mapping on vessels, exchangers and columns; encoded weld examination on new-build piping and vessels where the construction code and owner accept UT in place of radiographyNormally UT Level II first
Time of Flight Diffraction (TOFD)I, IIFlaw sizing on thick-wall vessel seams, heavy-wall fabrication and girth welds on offshore and pipeline work; often run with PAUTNormally UT Level II first
Radiographic Testing (RT)I, II, IIIFilm, CR and DR weld radiography on pipelines to API 1104, process piping to ASME B31.3, and shop-built vessels; profile radiography for corrosion under insulationNone for Level I training; radiation safety certification under Texas rules is a separate requirement (see below)
Magnetic Particle Testing (MT)I, II, IIIStructural steel to AWS D1.1 in fabrication yards, wet fluorescent MT on lifting gear, drill-stem and oilfield tubular inspection, crack checks on pump and compressor partsNone for Level I
Liquid Penetrant Testing (PT)I, II, IIIStainless and nickel-alloy welds in petrochemical units, valve and pump bodies, non-magnetic forgings, and precision parts for aerospace and space-sector contractors near Clear LakeNone for Level I
Visual Testing (VT)I, II, IIIWeld visual inspection to AWS D1.1, ASME and API 1104; pre- and post-turnaround visual checks; the foundation for every other methodNone for Level I
Eddy Current Testing (ET)I, II, IIIHeat-exchanger and condenser tube inspection during turnarounds, surface crack detection on non-ferrous and coated parts, conductivity sorting in aerospace workNone for Level I

Level III preparation covers the ASNT Basic examination and method examinations for candidates who will write procedures, approve techniques and examine Level I and II staff. See ASNT Level III training. Houston is an unusual market because so many companies need a Level III, either on staff or on contract. That is why Level III prep appears here alongside the technician courses.

Which course first? For a new entrant aiming at refinery and petrochemical work, VT, PT and MT give the quickest route onto a job ticket. UT is the long build that the best-paid Houston work depends on. PAUT and TOFD come after a solid UT Level II. For pipeline and fabrication work, RT and VT carry more weight. We will look at your target employers and suggest a sequence before you commit. Ask a Level III which course to take first.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Houston, step by step

  1. Your employer’s written practice. Every SNT-TC-1A certification starts here. The written practice defines the training hours, experience hours, examinations, vision requirements and recertification interval for each method and level. If you are an individual without an employer yet, your training records still count. The employer who hires you will certify you under its own document.
  2. Formal classroom training. You complete the method- and level-specific training hours the written practice sets. Atlantis delivers these live online or onsite, and issues training records showing the hours and topics covered per technician. The recommended minimums per method and level are listed in our NDT training requirements matrix. Use it rather than any hour figure quoted secondhand.
  3. Documented on-the-job experience. You log method experience and total NDT experience under a certified Level II or Level III. In Houston this usually means paid work on thickness surveys, weld inspection or fabrication QC. Experience, not classroom time, is almost always what decides how fast you reach Level II.
  4. General, specific and practical examinations. A Level III administers three exams. The general exam tests method theory. The specific exam tests the employer’s procedures, equipment and codes. The practical exam is hands-on work on real specimens with a documented checklist. Grading and minimum scores follow the written practice.
  5. Annual vision examination. Near-vision acuity and colour contrast are checked and recorded. Most written practices require this every year to keep a certification active.
  6. Certification by the employer. The employer’s certifying authority signs a record listing the method, level, date, exam results, training and experience. This record is what an owner-operator’s QA group or a third-party auditor asks for when your crew arrives at the gate.
  7. Recertification. Certifications expire on the interval your written practice sets. Renewal is by examination or by documented continuing performance, depending on the practice. We keep a recertification calendar for employer clients so certifications do not lapse in the middle of a turnaround.

For the employer side of this in more depth, see SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for Houston crews

Texas is big. A Houston inspection company might have technicians in Pasadena on Monday, at a Freeport terminal on Wednesday and on a Permian gathering line the next week. Centralised classroom training does not fit that pattern, so the delivery model is built around three formats.

  • Live online (instructor-led). Theory sessions are delivered live by an ASNT Level III-led team. Technicians attend from anywhere in Texas: Midland–Odessa, Corpus Christi, Beaumont–Port Arthur, San Antonio, Dallas–Fort Worth, the Rio Grande Valley or a rotation camp with a reliable connection. Sessions are interactive, questions are answered in real time, and attendance counts toward documented training hours where your written practice allows online classroom delivery.
  • Onsite at your facility. For crews of several technicians, we run the classroom and practical blocks at your shop, yard or plant training room, on your own equipment and on specimens that match what your people actually inspect. Onsite practicals are run under ASNT Level III oversight. This removes the travel cost and crew downtime that tuition quotes never show.
  • Blended. Theory is done online over a few weeks around rotations. The hands-on block and practical exam are then held onsite in one short, concentrated period. Most Houston contractors who train incumbent technicians end up here.

One honest limit: the practical examination cannot be taken online. It must be done hands-on, on real specimens, and witnessed and graded by a Level III. Online delivery covers theory and exam preparation. It does not replace the practical.

Scheduling works around the Gulf Coast calendar, not an academic term. Theory blocks can be placed in the shoulder months between turnaround seasons. Onsite practicals can be booked for when your crew is back from an outage. Night-shift crews and 14-and-14 rotations can take sessions at times that suit them. Send us the dates you cannot touch and we will build around them. Ask about onsite training for your Houston crew, or read about how live online NDT training works and corporate NDT programmes.

Where NDT technicians work in Houston

The Ship Channel refineries get most of the attention, but Houston NDT work is spread across more sectors than most candidates realise. Knowing which one you are aiming at changes which methods, codes and site requirements matter.

  • Refining and petrochemicals. Pasadena, Deer Park, Baytown, La Porte, Channelview and Texas City, plus the chemical complexes at Freeport and in Chambers County. The work is in-service inspection of piping, vessels, exchangers and tanks. The codes are ASME Section V for technique, ASME B31.3 and Section VIII for construction and repair, and the API inspection codes as context for the inspectors who use your data.
  • LNG and export terminals. Liquefaction and export facilities along the Texas coast, from Freeport to the Sabine Pass area, generate construction-phase weld inspection (RT, PAUT, VT) and later in-service programmes. Cryogenic stainless and nickel-steel welds put PT and UT technique skill at a premium.
  • Pipelines. Houston is the commercial headquarters of the US pipeline industry. New-construction girth welds are examined to API 1104. Intrastate pipeline safety in Texas is overseen by the Railroad Commission of Texas. Interstate lines fall under the federal PHMSA regulations. Pipeline operators also require operator qualification (OQ) for covered tasks. That is separate from NDT certification but often checked alongside it.
  • Oilfield equipment manufacturing. North and northwest Houston host a dense cluster of wellhead, pressure-control, drilling-tool and OCTG threading shops. MT, PT and UT dominate here. Many shops also work to drill-stem inspection standards such as DS-1 and to customer-specific API product specifications, which are context for the NDT technician rather than something Atlantis trains to.
  • Fabrication yards and module builders. Structural steel to AWS D1.1, pressure vessels to ASME Section VIII and offshore structures all need VT, MT, UT and RT on a production schedule.
  • Power generation. Large gas and coal-fired stations in the region, and the South Texas Project nuclear plant near Bay City. Nuclear in-service inspection runs under ASME Section XI and often needs performance-demonstration qualification beyond SNT-TC-1A. That is worth knowing before you target it.
  • Aerospace and space. NASA’s Johnson Space Center and the commercial space companies around Clear Lake and Ellington Field need PT, ET and UT on precision parts. That work usually runs under an aerospace personnel standard, which your employer will specify.

Radiography licensing in Texas. Texas is an NRC Agreement State. Industrial radiography is regulated by the Texas Department of State Health Services (DSHS) Radiation Control Program under 25 TAC §289.255, which was revised in 2024. Texas issues its own industrial radiographer certification. To get it, you complete a radiation safety course that meets the rule, then log documented on-the-job training as a trainee under a radiographer trainer authorised on a Texas licence or registration. This is separate from, and in addition to, your SNT-TC-1A RT certification. The NDT certificate says you can interpret a radiograph. The DSHS certification says you may work with a source or X-ray tube. Check the current DSHS requirements before you plan an RT career in Texas. Our RT course covers method and interpretation. It is not the state radiation safety course.

What Houston employers typically ask for, on top of the NDT card: a site safety orientation for the specific plant or industrial area, drug and alcohol screening, a Transportation Worker Identification Credential (TWIC) for work inside port and marine terminals regulated under the Maritime Transportation Security Act, and, on pipeline work, OQ for the covered tasks. None of these is NDT training, but all of them decide whether a certified technician can get to work on day one. Plan for them in your timeline.

Level III services and written practices for Houston NDT companies

Many Houston inspection companies started with a borrowed or outdated written practice and a Level III who has since left. That is the most common audit finding we see. When an owner-operator’s QA group audits your personnel records, they look at three things. They look at whether the written practice matches the current edition of SNT-TC-1A or CP-189 and the methods you actually perform. They look at whether every certification traces back to training, experience, exams and vision records. And they look at whether a named Level III approved the procedures.

Atlantis supports Houston employers with:

  • Written practice development or revision, fitted to your methods, levels, recertification choices and client requirements.
  • Level III services: procedure writing and approval, technique sheets, examination administration and grading, and certification record review. See SNT-TC-1A guidance for employers.
  • Pre-audit gap reviews before a major client audit or a new master services agreement.
  • Onboarding programmes for technicians recruited from other employers, whose previous certifications do not transfer and must be re-issued under your written practice.

This matters a lot for Houston companies that pick up technicians from other Gulf Coast contractors at the start of each turnaround season. A Level II from another employer is not your Level II until your Level III has checked the records, given your specific and practical exams, and signed your certification. Book a Level III consultation to review where your programme stands.

Practise before the practical exam

Many Houston candidates fail the practical, not the written. They know the theory but have not handled enough transducers, yokes and calibration blocks under exam pressure. Practical NDT, the Atlantis 3D simulator, lets trainees practise 12 methods in 5 environments: an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. The oil and gas site and storage tank scenes are close to what Houston technicians see every week. The welding workshop fits fabrication-yard candidates.

Use it to rehearse set-up order, scanning patterns, indication recognition and reporting before your practical session. Be clear about what it is. The simulator is practice only. It does not replace the practical exam on real specimens, and it does not count toward documented experience hours. For theory revision, work through the UT Level II practice questions and similar mock exams for your method.

Your instructor

Houston training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. He oversees course content, examinations and the Level III services described above. Houston is a code-heavy, audit-heavy market, and courses are built around the codes and client requirements Houston technicians actually face, not a generic syllabus. Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Houston

How do I get NDT certified in Houston?

Complete the formal training for your method and level, build documented on-the-job experience under a certified technician, and pass the general, specific and practical exams given by a Level III. Pass a vision exam, and your employer then certifies you under its SNT-TC-1A written practice. Training can be done online or onsite. The certification is issued by whoever employs you.

Can I take NDT training online from anywhere in Texas?

Yes. Theory is delivered as live, instructor-led online sessions, so a technician in Midland, Corpus Christi, Beaumont, Laredo or Lubbock attends the same class as one in Houston. Training records show the hours completed. The practical exam is the one part that cannot be done online. It is held hands-on on real specimens, usually onsite at the employer’s facility under Level III oversight. See how online NDT training works.

Do Houston employers accept online NDT training?

Under SNT-TC-1A, the employer’s written practice decides what training format it accepts. Many written practices allow instructor-led online classroom hours as long as the hours, content and attendance are documented. The practical training and exam are hands-on regardless. If you are unsure, ask the employer’s Level III, or send us their written practice and we will tell you whether online hours fit.

How long does UT Level 2 training take?

It depends on two things: the formal training hours your employer’s written practice requires for UT Level I and Level II, and the documented UT and total NDT experience you must build. The recommended figures are in our training requirements matrix. In practice the classroom is the short part. Experience hours are what take months, so start logging paid UT work as early as you can.

Do I need a license for radiography in Texas?

Yes, if you will handle sources or operate industrial X-ray equipment. Texas DSHS regulates industrial radiography under 25 TAC §289.255 and issues its own radiographer certification. You get it by completing a qualifying radiation safety course and documented trainee on-the-job training under an authorised radiographer trainer. That is on top of your SNT-TC-1A RT method certification. Check current DSHS requirements before you plan an RT route.

What does NDT training cost in Houston?

Pricing is quote on request. It depends on the method and level, the group size, and whether delivery is live online, onsite at your facility or blended. It also depends on whether you need Level III services such as a written practice or exam administration. Send us those details and we return cohort and onsite quotes within one business day. Get a Houston training quote.

Is ASNT certification recognised by Houston employers?

SNT-TC-1A is the framework most US refinery, petrochemical, pipeline and fabrication employers use to certify NDT personnel. Houston owner-operators and contractors routinely specify SNT-TC-1A or CP-189 in their contracts. Remember that under SNT-TC-1A the certification is issued by your employer, not by ASNT. ASNT also runs its own central certification programmes, which some Houston employers ask for in addition.

Can I get certified without an employer?

You can complete the training, keep your training records and prepare for the exams on your own. SNT-TC-1A certification, though, is issued by an employer under its written practice. Most individuals train first and are certified by the company that hires them. Some employers sponsor the training of new hires. That is worth asking about at interview.

Can you run training onsite at our Baytown, Pasadena or Freeport facility?

Yes. Onsite delivery is the main model for Houston crews. We run the classroom and practical blocks at your facility, on your equipment and specimens, under ASNT Level III oversight. We schedule around turnarounds and rotations.

Which NDT method should I learn first for Houston work?

For refinery and petrochemical in-service work, UT is the method that drives long-term demand. VT, PT and MT are quicker first certifications. For pipeline and new construction, RT and VT carry more weight. For oilfield equipment shops, MT and PT come first. Tell us the employers you are targeting and we will suggest a sequence.

Does Atlantis offer API 510, 570, 653 or CWI training?

No. Atlantis training is ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based only. Some Houston employers also ask for API inspector or AWS CWI credentials for senior inspection roles. Those are separate schemes with their own experience rules and exams, and we do not prepare candidates for them. We cover the NDT method training that sits underneath those roles.

Do I need a TWIC card to work as an NDT technician in Houston?

Only if your work takes you inside secure areas of port and marine terminals regulated under the Maritime Transportation Security Act, which many Ship Channel and coastal facilities are. It is a federal security credential, not an NDT qualification. Many Houston contractors expect new hires to have it or get it quickly.

Can our technicians use a simulator instead of real practice?

No. Practical NDT is a practice tool for rehearsing set-ups and indication recognition. It does not replace hands-on training on real equipment or the practical exam on real specimens, and it does not count as documented experience.
